task.title: Wake canonical-review-gate CI after the review-proof tag lands on approve

scope.owned_layer: The wake-up edge between a landed review-proof tag and the Canonical Review Gate workflow run that posts the required status: the workflow's workflow_dispatch entry point, the bridge's post-tag dispatch call on approve, and regression coverage for both halves.
scope.not_changing: Review policy itself (owner != reviewer, exact-head binding), the tag naming/push path, canonical_review_gate_ci.py's decision logic, ai_status.py's GITHUB_REVIEW_MODES and evidence matching, dev branch protection, and every non-approve decision path.

problem.observed: A task PR approved through the governed path kept mergeable_state BLOCKED even though the 'Pantheon canonical review gate' required context was listed as success.
problem.root_cause_1: GitHub pins the named required context to the identity that has historically posted it -- this workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated job run. github_review_bridge.py's _submit_required_status posts from a personal-token host process; the status appears in a plain status listing but does not move mergeable_state. Verified empirically against a live PR.
problem.root_cause_2: The review-proof tag is durable proof but is not an event this workflow listens for. None of opened/synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review fire from a bare tag push, so a PR approved with no further commits had no path to a re-run and would sit failing indefinitely.
problem.why_required_checks_sync_was_not_enough: SUP-CONFIG-REQUIRED-CHECKS-SYNC-20260805 restoring the gate to dev's required_status_checks was necessary but not sufficient; it fixed which context is demanded, not who posts it or when the workflow re-runs.

contract.workflow_dispatch_entry: canonical-review-gate.yml declares workflow_dispatch with required string inputs head_ref and head_sha, because a manual dispatch has no pull_request context to read the head from.
contract.input_precedence: HEAD_REF/HEAD_SHA resolve as github.event.inputs.<name> || github.event.pull_request.head.<field>, so the pull_request path is byte-for-byte unchanged when no inputs are supplied.
contract.concurrency: The group key falls back to head_sha on a dispatch run (no pull_request.number), so concurrent approvals for different heads do not cancel each other under cancel-in-progress.
contract.dispatch_trigger: bridge_review_decision dispatches the workflow exactly once, only when decision == approve, and only after _push_review_proof_tag has returned -- the workflow must never be woken to look for a tag that does not exist yet.
contract.best_effort: A dispatch failure is swallowed (GitHubReviewBridgeError only). The tag is the durable proof; a transient API error must not turn a real, recorded approval into an error, and the next natural push re-runs the gate anyway.

verification.result: no regression in the adjacent review-merge gate suite

regression_tests.name: test_approve_dispatches_canonical_review_gate_workflow
regression_tests.asserts: exactly one dispatch, ref == task branch, inputs == {head_ref, head_sha} bound to the reviewed head

regression_tests.name: test_reopen_does_not_dispatch_canonical_review_gate_workflow
regression_tests.asserts: no dispatch on a non-approve decision

regression_tests.name: test_approve_survives_a_failed_workflow_dispatch
regression_tests.asserts: approve still returns its mode and review_proof_ref when the dispatch API call raises

regression_tests.name: WorkflowDispatchContractTests
regression_tests.asserts: the bridge's workflow-file constant matches the real file name, the dispatched input names match the workflow's declared inputs, the pull_request types are still declared, and the env/concurrency fallbacks are exactly the dispatch-aware expressions

operational_notes: GitHub only honours workflow_dispatch for a workflow that exists on the repository default branch. The default branch here is dev, so the dispatch call 404s until this PR merges into dev; it is swallowed as best-effort until then. The first approval that actually benefits is the first one after this merge.

The dispatch targets binding.head_branch as the ref, so the run checks out the task branch and the gate job's own check run attaches to the reviewed head -- which is exactly the identity-attributed artifact branch protection is waiting for.
This PR's own gate check is expected to read FAILURE until the reviewer approves and the tag lands; that is the gate working, not a defect.
